content:
Ellen Lloyd – AncientPages.com – Parts I and II of this series examined ancient sightings and the physical and mechanical descriptions of so-called fire dragons across various cultures. We considered how distant civilizations described similar mechanical behaviors using comparable imagery. We also questioned why historical accounts reference iron shields, heavy chainmail, and other unfamiliar metallic sounds.

We reviewed a notable passage from The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle describing intense lightning and fiery dragons in flight, along with other ancient sources reporting similar sightings of flying dragons and unusual metallic sounds.

Part 3 will address the flight physics of antiquity and the biological impossibility of such creatures. We will also once again consider whether some ancient dragon sightings may have been misidentified as unidentified flying objects (UAP, Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena). As always, you are encouraged to draw your own conclusions regarding these historical accounts.

Welcome to a new weekly investigative series, Fire Dragons, UAPs And Ancient Mechanical Monsters, in which we will explore whether the ancient world mistook unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAPs) for fierce flying dragons.

As always, we will objectively bridge the gap between mainstream history and ancient mysteries by examining alternative theories without compromising academic integrity. It is a series suitable for history buffs, mythology lovers, and paranormal enthusiasts.

Now, let us begin our journey!
